general_information.Description: Demonstrate basic foundational principles, recognize second or foreign language learning theories, and design and plan lessons to teach English as a second or foreign language effectively. This specialization is the first of two specializations that make up the TESOL Certificate from Arizona State University. In this specialization, students will learn about the basic foundational principles of language acquisition and the basic techniques founded upon those principles. It will describe second or foreign language theories, and basic studies in second language acquisition and their pedagogical implications. It will elaborate upon basic design for lesson plans and provide access to professional resources. In the final Capstone Project, in collaboration with Arizona State University’s Global Launch, students will apply the skills they learned by designing a lesson plan which includes learning outcomes, assessments, materials, classroom management techniques and the learning activities themselves. When completing this specialization, students are eligible to continute the second specialization in order to complete the TESOL certificate experience.
general_information.StudentTasks: 1. Join the online course (spec.) when being invited by the admin. 2. Enroll in each MOOC of spec., regularly study MOOCs at least 5hrs/week by watching videos, reading materials, taking quizzes, doing assgnments... as required 3. Respect the Coursera Code of Conduct, at https://learner.coursera.help/hc/en-us/articles/208280036-Coursera-Code-of-Conduct 3. Keep online learning progress promptly (bonus will be awarded) 4. Communicate and discuss in forum 5. Attend off-line sessions in the Campus (Optional) 6. Must complete all MOOCs of spec. with certification in order to take the Final Exam at Campus
general_information.Note: 1) Ongoing assessment: Students who complete all MOOCs before the course deadline will receive 1 bonus point; otherwise, no bonus point will be awarded. 2) Theoretical Exam (TE) 3) Final Result (FR) =min (10, TE + Bonus) 4) Completion Criteria: TE>=4 and FR>=5

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Identify, summarize, and evaluate 7 basic language learning paradigms; and understand basic techniques founded on the principles.
Understand second or foreign language theories and practices for teaching and assessing listening, speaking, and pronunciation; and develop recognition of the importance of teaching philosophy.

Understand the cohesion between lesson design and teaching philosophies; Know how to design lesson plans based on principles and have knowledge of learning objectives, assessment plans, methods, materials, and learning activities.
Apply the skills to analyze lessons; identify teaching philosophy; build a five-day lesson plan, and a teaching tip.
